comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — PROJECT DATABASE

Map index + backup store + schema versions. The runmap folds `migrations.ts`
into this file; see SCHEMA below for why there is nothing to migrate yet.

Foundation 1: "Keep a database in the project folder that will be included in
the compile. Map index + the app's backup of the actual files. So files on
disk are what you see and edit; the database is what the app restores from
and diffs against."

WHY JSON AND NOT SQLITE — A2's call, flagged for Brandon.

A0 deliberately left `dependencies` empty and left the storage engine to this
phase. The database is canonical JSON on disk, written through
`taxonomy.canonicalJson`, for three reasons that come straight off the spec:

  1. Guideline 6 wants byte-identical output from identical input. A SQLite
     file is not byte-stable — page layout, free lists and vacuum state all
     drift — so every save would show a diff the user did not cause.
     `canonicalJson` sorts keys and spells `undefined` as `null` precisely so
     two equal states serialize to equal bytes. A1 wrote it for this.
  2. Foundation 1 says the database is "included in the compile" — it travels
     with the project folder. A text file survives being copied, zipped,
     versioned and read by a human. A binary needs the app to be legible.
  3. A native SQLite binding has to be rebuilt against every Electron ABI.
     That is a build hazard bought for a store that holds one document.

If the project ever outgrows a single JSON document, this is the file that
changes and nothing else — every other service goes through the functions
below rather than touching the disk.

Guideline 15: "Future-version compatibility is not addressed until the future

So the number is RECORDED and checked, and there are no migrations, because

comments.text:
Foundation 5: "Versioned diffs for the library and backups."

Every save takes a backup FIRST, then replaces the live database atomically.
Order matters: if the machine dies between the two, the backup exists and the
live file is still the previous good one. The reverse order can lose both.

Backups are append-only. Nothing in `backups/` is ever rewritten or removed —
they are written with an exclusive create, so a name collision fails rather
than replacing a snapshot.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — FILESYSTEM

Finder pick, project path resolution, and write-beside. The runmap merges
`paths.ts` and `atomic-write.ts` into this file.

THIS IS THE FILE WHERE A PLAUSIBLE-LOOKING BUG DESTROYS THE USER'S WORK.
Two rules govern every function in it.

GUIDELINE 20 — "Every export is a new file written beside existing files.
Exports never overwrite anything."

  `taxonomy.writeBesideName` picks a free name from a SNAPSHOT of a
  directory listing. A snapshot is not a guarantee: between the listing and
  the write, anything on the machine can create that file. So no function
  here trusts a name check. Every create goes through `O_EXCL` — `wx` for a
  file, non-recursive `mkdir` for a directory — which is the kernel refusing
  to clobber, not this code promising not to. If the name is taken we get
  `EEXIST` and step aside; we never truncate.

  There is no function in this file that opens a user file for writing
  without `O_EXCL`. `atomicReplace` is the one overwriting write, it is
  private, and it is reachable only through two fenced entry points:
  `writeFileAtomic` (restricted to a project's own database folder by
  `assertAppOwned`) and `writeAppSettingsFileAtomic` (restricted to the app's
  own settings folder — A4-crossing, see that function).

CONTAINMENT — a docset label is user text. `screenLabel` rejects `/` and
  NUL, but it does NOT reject `..`, so a folder labelled `..` resolves to a
  path outside the export root. Every path built from user text goes through
  `resolveWithin`, which refuses anything that escapes. See A2's findings.

ELECTRON: this module is deliberately importable WITHOUT Electron. The only
Electron call (`pickFolder`) imports it dynamically at call time, so the
tests can exercise the dangerous code against a real temp directory without
booting an app.

comments.text:
ROLLBACK IS THE ONLY REASON THESE TWO FUNCTIONS EXIST.

Brandon's call, 2026-08-27: "No partial exports survive on disk, ever." A
failed export must delete everything it wrote this run and be treated as if
it never ran. That overrides the leave-it-and-report behaviour built first.

Deleting is the operation that loses work when it is aimed one directory too
high, so both functions below are deliberately the WEAKEST tools that do the
job:

  - `removeFileIfPresent` unlinks ONE named file. It does not recurse, does
    not glob, and does not take a directory.
  - `removeDirectoryIfEmpty` uses `rmdir`, which REFUSES a non-empty
    directory. If anything the export did not create is sitting inside, the
    kernel declines and the folder stays.

There is no recursive delete anywhere in this codebase. The caller
(`export-service`) tracks the exact paths it created and hands them back one
at a time; nothing is inferred from a directory listing.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — IPC REGISTRATION

Wires one handler to every channel in the contract.

THREE THINGS THIS FILE GUARANTEES STRUCTURALLY:

  1. Every channel has a handler. `Handlers` is a mapped type over
     `IpcChannel`, so a missing channel is a compile error here rather than a
     silent hang in the renderer three phases later.
  2. Nothing escapes as an exception. Every handler is wrapped; a throw comes
     back as `ok: false` with a code from the contract. An unhandled rejection
     across the IPC boundary would reach the renderer as a stringified stack.
  3. Guideline 16: `discrepancies` is on the envelope and is always an array.
     A handler cannot succeed "quietly" while something was renamed, replaced,
     emptied or stepped aside — the flags travel on success and failure alike.

`ipcMain` is a PARAMETER, not an import. This module never pulls Electron in
at load time, so the wiring can be exercised without booting an app.

to a FLAG. With the app's `docgen/` now inside the map folder, the
name it collides with is any TOP-LEVEL child of the root — which the
user can rename into at any time, long after the map was created, so a

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — PRELOAD BRIDGE

The typed bridge. This is the only place the renderer can reach the main
process, and it exposes exactly the contract and nothing else.

WHY THE CHANNEL IS CHECKED AGAINST A LIST

`invoke` is typed to `IpcChannel`, but types are a compile-time promise and
this function sits at the boundary where untrusted renderer code runs. A
renderer that has been compromised — or a bug that builds a channel name from
a string — could pass anything at all. So the name is checked against the
runtime `IPC_CHANNELS` list before it is forwarded, and an unknown channel
comes back as a normal `ok: false` result rather than reaching `ipcMain`.

FOUNDATION 4: there is no channel here that runs anything, because there is
no such channel in the contract. This file cannot widen that surface — it can
only forward names the contract already lists.

Built as CommonJS on purpose (see `electron.vite.config.ts`): Electron does
not load an ESM preload when the renderer is sandboxed.

BRANDON'S RULING, 2026-08-28: "it shouldn't create a named folder inside the
container until export." Nothing is written into a container folder until
`export-service.ts` runs — that is the only place a named map folder
appears on disk. So a map's LIVE data cannot live in a folder the user
picked; it lives here, in the app's own Map Library, beside the settings
file (the one place `settings-service.ts` says the app is allowed
app-level state).

ONE SUBFOLDER PER MAP, NAMED BY A GENERATED ID — Brandon's answer, verbatim,
to "one subfolder per map, or one combined file?" A map's own folder reuses
every path/database primitive `fs.ts` and `db/project-db.ts` already have
for a project root — `docgen/database.json`, `schema.json`, `backups/`,
`library-backup/` — nothing new to learn there. The id is generated
(`crypto.randomUUID()`), never the map's own name: the map can be renamed
at will (Guideline 7 — the app does not name the user's work) and the
library's bookkeeping must not care.

NO INDEX FILE. "The library holds the maps," not a list of where they are.
`listMapLibrary` is a directory listing, read the same way a container
folder was always read for Load Map: each subfolder is recognised by its
OWN `docgen/database.json`, never by guessing from a name. A combined index
would be a second place a map's name could drift from its database; this
way there is only ever the one.

EXPORT RECORDS live beside each map's own database, for the same reason:
one small file per map, not a combined one. It is the app's OWN bookkeeping
(never the user's), so it is simply overwritten on every export — it holds
the LAST export, not a history. Foundation 1: report, never reconcile — if
the folder it points at is gone, `listMapLibrary` says so; it does not
chase it down or drop the map from the list.

Phase 4. Root component, mounted here (index.html's comment: "A4 owns
App.tsx and it must mount React itself"). This file owns LAYOUT ONLY —
three vertical stacks, drawers, splitters, project tabs, and the
dimmed-behind-modal library overlay. The panels that fill each slot
(map canvas, docset file tree/preview, editor fields, library window) are
A5–A9's job; this file provides one clearly-named placeholder `<div>` per

LAYOUT, PER SPEC (line 3 + WINDOWS section)

  "Map is the whole screen, docset and editor are tabs on the sides that
  open drawers, user gets to adjust the width of the borders (3 vertical
  stacks for windows)."

Three vertical stacks, left to right: docset drawer, map (always full
height, always mounted), editor drawer. Each drawer has a persistent tab
strip at the outer edge (always visible, toggles the drawer) and, when
open, a resizable panel between the tab strip and the map, dragged via a
`Splitter`. The docset drawer's own panel splits horizontally per spec
line 12: file list above, completed-file preview below, adjustable border
height — a second `Splitter` on the y axis, local to that drawer.

LIBRARY OVERLAY, PER SPEC (line 3)

  "Settings/archive/script editor is separate screen entirely (pop out
  that can be dragged around to see the map screen, but map screen is a
  kinda dark and can't be clicked on except for modal button in the bottom
  corner of the map screen that says 'save' or 'cancel' and closes the
  movable screen)."

No IPC channel or event for "library window open" exists in
`shared/ipc-contract.ts` (checked before writing this — A8 has not run
yet, and no window-management channel is planned for it either per the
runmap, which keeps A8 to three `.tsx` files, all under
`src/renderer/library/`). Read literally, the "pop out" is not a second OS
window — it's a draggable overlay panel within this same renderer, moved
by its own header, sitting above a dimmed backdrop that blocks every
click on the map screen except the two modal buttons. `isLibraryOpen` and
the overlay's drag position are therefore local state owned by this shell,
not a store — there is nothing for a store to synchronize with yet.
Flagged in the receipt for Brandon.

The spec's ONLY stated behavior for the Save/Cancel buttons is that they
"close the movable screen" — nothing about what "save" persists, because
that's library-internal state (A8's). So both buttons just close the
overlay here; A8 will need its own hook into "did the user want to keep
what's open" if that turns out to matter, which is also flagged below.

SPLITTERS AND DRAWER STATE ARE LOCAL, NOT STORE STATE

No store owns "is the docset drawer open" or "how wide is it" — those are
pure window-chrome concerns, not domain data, and nothing downstream reads
them. Kept as local `useState` in this component, same category call as
A3's `AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`: arbitrary defaults, one constant each, cheap
to change.

PERSISTENCE — WIRED (A4-crossing, Brandon authorized the crossing)

Brandon's ruling: this state survives a reload, and per spec line 22
settings live in a findable plain-text file ("stored somewhere else as
normal text files I could find if I needed to with finder") — NOT
`localStorage` (an opaque blob in Electron's user-data folder, the opposite
of findable) and NOT the project database (spec line 28 fences that to the
map index and file backups, and it ships in the compile).

So this file no longer stores chrome itself: it holds ONE `AppLayoutSettings`
value, reads it once on mount through `settings:readLayout`, and writes it
back through `settings:writeLayout` on a debounce. `main/services/
settings-service.ts` owns the file — WHERE that file lives is still
Brandon's open call, behind one constant there.

THE DEFAULTS LIVE HERE, NOT IN MAIN. Main returns only the fields that
survived reading the file (`StoredLayoutSettings`, a partial), and this file
merges them over `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` below and clamps them to the same
min/max the splitters enforce. One place that knows what a legal drawer
width is, and it is the one that draws the drawer. A missing file, a
corrupt file, or a failed read all land in the same place: the defaults,
silently, with the app still starting.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST READ COMES BACK (`isLayoutLoaded`).
Writing on mount would overwrite Brandon's saved layout with the defaults in
the one frame before his real values arrive.

DIM SCOPE — MAP SCREEN ONLY (A4-fixes)

Brandon's ruling: the dimmed-behind-modal backdrop covers the map screen
(`.map-slot`) only, not the project tabs or either drawer — spec line 3's
"map screen is a kinda dark" is the map, not the whole working surface.
The backdrop and the Save/Cancel modal buttons are therefore rendered
INSIDE `.map-slot` (see `MapDimOverlay`), not as a full-viewport overlay.
The library window itself (the draggable pop-out) stays a top-level fixed
overlay — spec says it "can be dragged around to see the map screen",
which only makes sense if it can move over the drawers too.

CLOSE-TAB PROMPT — WIRED (A4-crossing, Brandon authorized the crossing)

Brandon ruled that closing a project tab prompts the same way new and load
prompt. A4-fixes found the door shut: `PromptingSaveAction` was
`Extract<SaveAction, 'new' | 'load'>` and `SaveAction` had no `'close'`
member, so the only way through was `confirmLoad` — which would show a
"load" prompt while closing a tab, and was rightly refused. `'close'` is now
a first-class `SaveAction` member (`shared/types.ts`) and
`save-model.confirmClose` is its ask, identical in shape to
`confirmNew`/`confirmLoad`. `handleCloseProject` goes through it, and the
tab is closed only after the ask resolves.

THE PROMPT UI IS MINIMAL AND INLINE-STYLED, ON PURPOSE — FLAGGED. Phase 9
owns `common/Dialogs.tsx` and it has not run; `save-model`'s `decide`
callback is where that dialog will eventually plug in. Until then the ask
needs SOMETHING on screen or it is not an ask, so `SavePromptDialog` below
is the smallest honest one: the two choices the contract allows
(`SavePrompt.choices`), a name box for the fork, and a Cancel that abandons
the close entirely. It carries its own inline styles rather than classes in
`theme.css` so that A9 can delete it whole without unpicking the stylesheet.

CANCEL IS NOT A THIRD CHOICE. `SaveModelChoice` has exactly two arms and the
contract has no "discard"; Cancel rejects out of `decide`, which means
nothing is saved AND nothing is closed — see `save-model.ts`'s note.

/**
 * DOC GENERATOR — APP SHELL
 *
 * Phase 4. Root component, mounted here (index.html's comment: "A4 owns
 * App.tsx and it must mount React itself"). This file owns LAYOUT ONLY —
 * three vertical stacks, drawers, splitters, project tabs, and the
 * dimmed-behind-modal library overlay. The panels that fill each slot
 * (map canvas, docset file tree/preview, editor fields, library window) are
 * A5–A9's job; this file provides one clearly-named placeholder `<div>` per
 * slot and nothing else — no panel logic, no panel state.
 *
 * LAYOUT, PER SPEC (line 3 + WINDOWS section)
 *
 *   "Map is the whole screen, docset and editor are tabs on the sides that
 *   open drawers, user gets to adjust the width of the borders (3 vertical
 *   stacks for windows)."
 *
 * Three vertical stacks, left to right: docset drawer, map (always full
 * height, always mounted), editor drawer. Each drawer has a persistent tab
 * strip at the outer edge (always visible, toggles the drawer) and, when
 * open, a resizable panel between the tab strip and the map, dragged via a
 * `Splitter`. The docset drawer's own panel splits horizontally per spec
 * line 12: file list above, completed-file preview below, adjustable border
 * height — a second `Splitter` on the y axis, local to that drawer.
 *
 * LIBRARY OVERLAY, PER SPEC (line 3)
 *
 *   "Settings/archive/script editor is separate screen entirely (pop out
 *   that can be dragged around to see the map screen, but map screen is a
 *   kinda dark and can't be clicked on except for modal button in the bottom
 *   corner of the map screen that says 'save' or 'cancel' and closes the
 *   movable screen)."
 *
 * No IPC channel or event for "library window open" exists in
 * `shared/ipc-contract.ts` (checked before writing this — A8 has not run
 * yet, and no window-management channel is planned for it either per the
 * runmap, which keeps A8 to three `.tsx` files, all under
 * `src/renderer/library/`). Read literally, the "pop out" is not a second OS
 * window — it's a draggable overlay panel within this same renderer, moved
 * by its own header, sitting above a dimmed backdrop that blocks every
 * click on the map screen except the two modal buttons. `isLibraryOpen` and
 * the overlay's drag position are therefore local state owned by this shell,
 * not a store — there is nothing for a store to synchronize with yet.
 * Flagged in the receipt for Brandon.
 *
 * The spec's ONLY stated behavior for the Save/Cancel buttons is that they
 * "close the movable screen" — nothing about what "save" persists, because
 * that's library-internal state (A8's). So both buttons just close the
 * overlay here; A8 will need its own hook into "did the user want to keep
 * what's open" if that turns out to matter, which is also flagged below.
 *
 * SPLITTERS AND DRAWER STATE ARE LOCAL, NOT STORE STATE
 *
 * No store owns "is the docset drawer open" or "how wide is it" — those are
 * pure window-chrome concerns, not domain data, and nothing downstream reads
 * them. Kept as local `useState` in this component, same category call as
 * A3's `AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`: arbitrary defaults, one constant each, cheap
 * to change.
 *
 * PERSISTENCE — WIRED (A4-crossing, Brandon authorized the crossing)
 *
 * Brandon's ruling: this state survives a reload, and per spec line 22
 * settings live in a findable plain-text file ("stored somewhere else as
 * normal text files I could find if I needed to with finder") — NOT
 * `localStorage` (an opaque blob in Electron's user-data folder, the opposite
 * of findable) and NOT the project database (spec line 28 fences that to the
 * map index and file backups, and it ships in the compile).
 *
 * So this file no longer stores chrome itself: it holds ONE `AppLayoutSettings`
 * value, reads it once on mount through `settings:readLayout`, and writes it
 * back through `settings:writeLayout` on a debounce. `main/services/
 * settings-service.ts` owns the file — WHERE that file lives is still
 * Brandon's open call, behind one constant there.
 *
 * THE DEFAULTS LIVE HERE, NOT IN MAIN. Main returns only the fields that
 * survived reading the file (`StoredLayoutSettings`, a partial), and this file
 * merges them over `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` below and clamps them to the same
 * min/max the splitters enforce. One place that knows what a legal drawer
 * width is, and it is the one that draws the drawer. A missing file, a
 * corrupt file, or a failed read all land in the same place: the defaults,
 * silently, with the app still starting.
 *
 * NOTHING IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST READ COMES BACK (`isLayoutLoaded`).
 * Writing on mount would overwrite Brandon's saved layout with the defaults in
 * the one frame before his real values arrive.
 *
 * DIM SCOPE — MAP SCREEN ONLY (A4-fixes)
 *
 * Brandon's ruling: the dimmed-behind-modal backdrop covers the map screen
 * (`.map-slot`) only, not the project tabs or either drawer — spec line 3's
 * "map screen is a kinda dark" is the map, not the whole working surface.
 * The backdrop and the Save/Cancel modal buttons are therefore rendered
 * INSIDE `.map-slot` (see `MapDimOverlay`), not as a full-viewport overlay.
 * The library window itself (the draggable pop-out) stays a top-level fixed
 * overlay — spec says it "can be dragged around to see the map screen",
 * which only makes sense if it can move over the drawers too.
 *
 * CLOSE-TAB PROMPT — WIRED (A4-crossing, Brandon authorized the crossing)
 *
 * Brandon ruled that closing a project tab prompts the same way new and load
 * prompt. A4-fixes found the door shut: `PromptingSaveAction` was
 * `Extract<SaveAction, 'new' | 'load'>` and `SaveAction` had no `'close'`
 * member, so the only way through was `confirmLoad` — which would show a
 * "load" prompt while closing a tab, and was rightly refused. `'close'` is now
 * a first-class `SaveAction` member (`shared/types.ts`) and
 * `save-model.confirmClose` is its ask, identical in shape to
 * `confirmNew`/`confirmLoad`. `handleCloseProject` goes through it, and the
 * tab is closed only after the ask resolves.
 *
 * THE PROMPT UI IS MINIMAL AND INLINE-STYLED, ON PURPOSE — FLAGGED. Phase 9
 * owns `common/Dialogs.tsx` and it has not run; `save-model`'s `decide`
 * callback is where that dialog will eventually plug in. Until then the ask
 * needs SOMETHING on screen or it is not an ask, so `SavePromptDialog` below
 * is the smallest honest one: the two choices the contract allows
 * (`SavePrompt.choices`), a name box for the fork, and a Cancel that abandons
 * the close entirely. It carries its own inline styles rather than classes in
 * `theme.css` so that A9 can delete it whole without unpicking the stylesheet.
 *
 * CANCEL IS NOT A THIRD CHOICE. `SaveModelChoice` has exactly two arms and the
 * contract has no "discard"; Cancel rejects out of `decide`, which means
 * nothing is saved AND nothing is closed — see `save-model.ts`'s note.

files and folders"). Owns the editable filetree: add / rename / delete /

WINDOWS: "Use tags on folders to tag and coordinate with nodes"), and
click-to-select for `FilePreview.tsx` in the slot below.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN
  - The split between file list and preview — A4's `Splitter` +
    `docsetListHeight` in `App.tsx` already does this; this file is the
    top half's content only, not a second split.
  - The completed-file text and its tag editor — `FilePreview.tsx`, mounted
    separately into the slot below. This file only tracks and exposes
    WHICH node is selected, via `usePreviewSelection` below.
  - Template authoring/attachment — `editor-store.ts`'s `attachTemplate` /
    `detachTemplate` is Phase 7's surface. A file added here is always a
    Foundation-2 plain file (`templateId: null`) until the editor attaches
    one; `FilePreview.tsx` still renders it correctly either way.
  - Character screening enforcement beyond this UI — `docset-store.ts`'s
    own header says screening a label is "a live-typing UI concern... for
    a later phase's input component to call before it ever reaches this
    store." `LabelField` below is that component: it blocks Save on any
    Guideline-18 ERROR and shows WARNINGs inline, but does not build the
    full "this file / this happened / possible outcomes / deterministic
    choices" discrepancy block — that shared shape is Phase 9's
    `common/Dialogs.tsx`.

STYLING: no new CSS file — `theme.css` is outside this fence. A4's
`.docset-file-list-slot` centers/italicizes as a PLACEHOLDER style; this
component overrides it with an inline style on its own root, the same
precedent A5 set for `.map-slot`.

A7 ADDED TWO THINGS HERE
  - A per-folder ROLE select (`docsetStore.setNodeRole`). Role decides
    whether a folder is a map node and whether it has a job path, so a
    folder created under the wrong one used to need delete-and-recreate,
    which destroys its children. Root is excluded: it is always `global`.
  - DRAG-AND-DROP reorder, on native HTML5 drag events and no dependency
    (`package.json`'s `dependencies` stays empty). See DRAG STATE below for
    what counts as a valid drop; everything else is a silent no-op, never
    an error. The ↑/↓ buttons are KEPT — same mutator, and they are the
    keyboard-reachable path that dragging is not.

DOCSET-ICONS TASK SUPERSEDES A7's ROLE SELECT AND MOVES THE DRAG HANDLE
  - A7's role `<select>` (four options, `[role]` text badge on the root) is
    GONE. Every row now shows a LEADING KIND ICON (folder glyph / blank-page
    glyph, inline SVG — `FolderIcon`/`FileIcon` below) with three behaviors,
    Brandon's words: click it swaps file<->folder
    (`docsetStore.swapNodeKind`); click the NAME selects the row (unchanged
    from A6); click-and-hold the icon drags, and a fired drag NULLS the
    swap — see `handleIconClick`'s `suppressSwapRef` guard below for how.
  - Folders (never the root — it stays pinned to `global`, no control at
    all) get a binary JOB TOGGLE in the role select's old spot instead:
    on = `role: 'job'`, off = the folder's remembered previous non-job role
    (`toggleFolderJobRole` below), defaulting to `'sequence'` when nothing
    was remembered yet. This is Brandon's pick to make, not this agent's —
    see the receipt's DECISIONS for the default and why.
  - THE DRAG HANDLE MOVED from the name span (A7's choice) to the icon span
    — Brandon's spec puts hold-to-drag on the icon specifically, so

DOC GENERATOR — FILE PREVIEW

Phase 6. Two mount sites:

  1. `App.tsx`'s `.docset-file-preview-slot` — spec line 12: "click a file
     to see what the file will look like when completed". Mounted with no
     props: it reads the active project itself and is CONTROLLED by
     `DocsetPanel.tsx`'s `usePreviewSelection` — the docset tree above IS
     the picker, so this component renders no picker of its own here.

  2. `MapCanvas.tsx`'s job drawer, `data-slot="job-drawer-preview"` —
     Guideline 23's job view has no tree to click through, so when the
     `candidates` prop is passed this component renders its own small
     picker over that job's fileset (every file along the job's path)
     before previewing one, with its own uncontrolled selection.

"Completed" means `taxonomy.renderDocument(template, content)` — the exact
function `main/services/export-service.ts` calls to write the real file, so
what this shows is never a second, separately-invented preview of what the
file will contain (Guideline 6: same input, same output).

Falls back to a blank `FileContent` (matching `editor-store.ts`'s own
`blankContent` shape) when nothing has been typed yet — `editor-store`
returns `null` rather than inventing one, and this is the one place that
needs a value to hand `renderDocument`, not a change to what `editor-store`
reports.

with nodes". Works on the selected node whether it is a file or a folder;
a folder gets tags only, since a folder is not a document and has nothing

Phase 7. Mounts into A4's `.editor-panel-slot` (App.tsx's `EditorDrawerPanel`).
Foundation 7: "the editor is where the files are edited or attached to the

DOC GENERATOR — FIELD INPUTS

Phase 7's second file. Owns the actual input WIDGETS `EditorPanel.tsx`
renders per segment — this file has no opinion on field ORDER (that's
`editor-store.ts`'s `getOrderedFieldViews`, which `EditorPanel.tsx` walks)
and no opinion on which template is attached (also `EditorPanel.tsx`).

Spec, Editor window:
  - "Text input boxes for the parts that need to change"
  - "Some can be free text"
  - "Some can be straight up file attachments which include the scripts
     (which would show up as text anyways, some of them could be dragged
     and dropped in and some could be imported from the app's saved
     scripts)"

FOUR WIDGETS, matching `TemplateSegment`/`InputKind` (shared/types.ts)
exactly — nothing invented beyond what the kernel already models:
  - `FixedTextView`      a `FixedTextSegment` — read-only, never editable
                         here. Guideline 2: fixed text is prefilled by the
                         template author, not the person filling the file in.
  - `PlainTextField`     Foundation 2: a regular (template-less) file is
                         just a single text input field.
  - `TextFieldInput`     an `InputFieldSegment` with `inputKind: 'text'`.
  - `AttachmentFieldInput` an `InputFieldSegment` with `inputKind:
                         'attachment'`. Every write goes through
                         `editorStore.setAttachmentValue`, which stores
                         `AttachmentValue.text` — "would show up as text
                         anyways" — so this is a text box with two extra
                         ways to fill it (drop a file, or pick a saved
                         script), not a second kind of value.

WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT OWN
  - Attaching/detaching a TEMPLATE — `EditorPanel.tsx`, via
    `editorStore.attachTemplate`/`detachTemplate` (A7 Fix C: those two
    functions are the only place `DocsetFile.templateId` may be written).
  - Character screening on typed field VALUES — Guideline 18 is a LABEL
    concern (`taxonomy.screenLabel`, used by `docset/DocsetPanel.tsx`'s
    `LabelField` for node names). Field values are free text with no
    filesystem meaning, so nothing here screens them.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — IPC CLIENT

The typed wrapper over `main/preload.ts`'s bridge. Nothing else in the
renderer is allowed to touch `window.docGenerator` directly — every store in
`state.ts` goes through `invoke`/`call`/`onEvent` here.

GUIDELINE 16, THE PART THAT LIVES HERE

`IpcResult` always carries `discrepancies`, on success and failure alike.
That envelope is only as good as the promise that nothing built on top of it
drops the array on the floor. This file is where that promise is kept: every
`invoke()` feeds its `discrepancies` into a single feed, and the
`discrepancy:raised` event (for anything flagged outside a request the
renderer made) feeds the same one. Phase 9's `common/Dialogs.tsx` is the
eventual UI for this feed; this file only guarantees nothing reaches that UI
having already been quietly discarded.

The event listener is wired LAZILY, on the first `subscribeDiscrepancies`
call, not at module load. Importing this file must be side-effect-free —
under vitest (no bridge, no `window.docGenerator`) or during any renderer
bootstrap ordering, importing the module should never throw. Only calling
into it should.

DOC GENERATOR — LIBRARY WINDOW

Phase 8's first file. Spec: "the most underdeveloped window[]" — Brandon is
fine with that, and this file does not try to outgrow it.

SETTLED SHAPE, NOT REOPENED HERE: A4 already built the pop-out — an
in-renderer draggable overlay (`App.tsx`'s `LibraryWindow` function, the
drag header, `.library-window` CSS) with the map dimmed behind it
(`MapDimOverlay`) and Save/Cancel as two modal buttons in the map's bottom
corner. This file is the CONTENT mounted into that overlay's
`.library-window-slot` (`data-slot="library-window"`) — not a second
window, not new IPC for window management, not a redesign. `App.tsx`'s own
top-level function is also named `LibraryWindow`; the mount aliases the
import (`LibraryWindowContent`) rather than touch that file beyond the one
import + one slot-body line the fence allows.

SAVE/CANCEL — what A4's two modal buttons actually do today (per its own
file header): both just close the overlay. `library-store.ts`'s own header
explains why nothing here needed a buffered save: "READ-THROUGH, NOT
LOCAL-THEN-SAVED... every `library:*` write handler ALREADY persists to
disk and returns the resulting value before this store ever sees it."
Every action below (pick a folder, resolve a foreign file, fork a version)
commits the moment its own button is pressed — the same immediate-commit
pattern `docset/DocsetPanel.tsx`'s `LabelField`/tag editor/role select
already established. Closing the overlay (either modal button) simply
stops editing; there is nothing buffered to roll back, so "Cancel"
doing exactly what "Save" does is correct here, not a gap this file needs
to close. `ScriptEditor.tsx`'s propose/commit/discard flow (Guideline 5)
is the one place a DRAFT exists before it is persisted, and it owns its
own explicit commit/discard, independent of the overlay's buttons.

SETTINGS FOLDER PICKERS — Foundation 1 / Guideline 21: "a folder picked
from settings, through the Finder." The IPC channel already exists
end-to-end (`dialog:pickFolder`, `FolderPurpose = 'library-folder'`,

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — GRAPH LAYOUT

The runmap calls this "the hardest single file: layout must be byte-stable
across runs or Guideline 6 dies quietly". Quietly is the operative word.
Nondeterminism here throws no error and crashes nothing — the map simply
draws itself slightly differently on Tuesday, and the user stops trusting
that a difference was their own doing. Guideline 6 is the whole product.

WHAT THIS FILE IS

A pure function. `layoutGraph(graph)` takes the `MapGraph` that
`state/map-store.ts` derived from the docset and returns pixel geometry.
No I/O, no clock, no randomness, no globals, no React, no DOM.

WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT

It does not decide WHICH job connects to which. `deriveMapGraph` in
`state/map-store.ts` settled that (one chain across the depth-first,
authoring-order walk) and this file builds on exactly that edge model
without redefining it. Every edge here is looked up by id against the node
list; nothing re-derives structure.

It also does not know about flags, selection, hover, or discrepancies.
Those change without the docset changing, so folding them in would break
"same docset in, same layout out" by design. Flag counts are computed in
`MapCanvas.tsx` and handed to the renderers alongside this geometry.

It does not read `graph.style`. Cable and notch are two renderers over ONE
geometry — switching style must not move a single node. That is deliberate.

------------------------------------------------------------------
NONDETERMINISM AUDIT — every source considered, and how each is closed
------------------------------------------------------------------

 1. CLOCK — nothing in this file can observe time: no clock read of any
    kind, from the date object, the timer, or the performance counter.
    Enforced by a source grep in `tests/determinism.test.ts`, the same way
    `taxonomy.ts` is enforced. (The banned identifiers are spelled out in
    that test's `forbidden` list, and deliberately NOT spelled out here —
    naming them in a comment fails the grep, which is the test doing its
    job rather than a false alarm.)

 2. RANDOMNESS — no dice, from the math library or from the platform's
    secure-random source. Same grep, and its `forbidden` list names both.

 3. SET / MAP ITERATION ORDER — a `Map` is used for id lookup only and is
    never iterated to produce output. The one `Set` (unique depths) is
    drained into an array and then EXPLICITLY sorted numerically, so its
    insertion order cannot reach the result.

 4. `Object.keys()` ORDER — never used. Nothing in the output is built by
    walking an object's keys.

 5. LOCALE — locale-aware string comparison and the whole
    internationalization API are BANNED here. They vary with ICU build and
    host locale, which is exactly the "different machine, different bytes"
    failure this file exists to prevent. Id ties break on `compareIds`,
    plain UTF-16 code-unit comparison. (Same grep, same reason as 1.)

 6. SORT STABILITY — never relied on. Every comparator is TOTAL: it falls
    through to the node id, which is unique, so no two elements ever
    compare equal and the engine's tie handling is unreachable.

 7. FLOAT ACCUMULATION — there is none. No coordinate is ever computed by
    adding a step to the previous coordinate. Every one is
    `origin + index * step` from integer constants, so the value depends on
    the index alone and not on how many nodes were summed before it.

 8. NEGATIVE ZERO — `Math.round(-0.2)` is `-0`, which is `!== 0` under
    `Object.is` and can flip a snapshot comparison for no visible reason.
    `snap()` normalizes it away.

 9. NON-FINITE INPUT — a `NaN` or `Infinity` depth would poison every
    downstream coordinate and propagate silently. `finiteDepth()` clamps
    to a deterministic integer instead.

10. INPUT ARRAY ORDER — split deliberately in two:

      `graph.nodes` order IS meaningful and IS preserved. It is the user's
      authoring order, and `tests/determinism.test.ts` already states the
      rule: "does NOT ignore array order — arrangement is the user's".
      Node ordinal is array index, on purpose.

      `graph.edges` order is NOT meaningful. Edges are derived from the
      node walk, so their array position carries nothing the node list does
      not already say. Edges are therefore deduplicated and sorted on an
      explicit total key before any geometry is computed. Shuffling the
      edge array is byte-identical — covered by a test.

11. DUPLICATE NODE IDS — `deriveMapGraph` cannot produce them today (folder
    ids are unique), but the type permits it. First occurrence wins for
    edge lookup; every node still gets its own ordinal from its own index.
    Documented rather than thrown on, because a layout that throws takes
    the whole map down over a drawing detail.

12. DANGLING EDGES — an edge naming a job that is not in `nodes` is dropped,
    deterministically, and counted in `dropped` so the caller can see it
    rather than wonder where a cable went.

Every number this file emits is an integer. That is not decoration: it is
what makes the output survive a JSON round trip byte for byte, with no
float formatting to argue about. `tests/determinism.test.ts` asserts it.

 *
 * A pure function. `layoutGraph(graph)` takes the `MapGraph` that
 * `state/map-store.ts` derived from the docset and returns pixel geometry.
 * No I/O, no clock, no randomness, no globals, no React, no DOM.
 *
 * WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT
 *
 * It does not decide WHICH job connects to which. `deriveMapGraph` in
 * `state/map-store.ts` settled that (one chain across the depth-first,
 * authoring-order walk) and this file builds on exactly that edge model
 * without redefining it. Every edge here is looked up by id against the node
 * list; nothing re-derives structure.
 *
 * It also does not know about flags, selection, hover, or discrepancies.
 * Those change without the docset changing, so folding them in would break
 * "same docset in, same layout out" by design. Flag counts are computed in
 * `MapCanvas.tsx` and handed to the renderers alongside this geometry.
 *
 * It does not read `graph.style`. Cable and notch are two renderers over ONE
 * geometry — switching style must not move a single node. That is deliberate.
 *
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------
 * NONDETERMINISM AUDIT — every source considered, and how each is closed
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 *  1. CLOCK — nothing in this file can observe time: no clock read of any
 *     kind, from the date object, the timer, or the performance counter.
 *     Enforced by a source grep in `tests/determinism.test.ts`, the same way
 *     `taxonomy.ts` is enforced. (The banned identifiers are spelled out in
 *     that test's `forbidden` list, and deliberately NOT spelled out here —
 *     naming them in a comment fails the grep, which is the test doing its
 *     job rather than a false alarm.)
 *
 *  2. RANDOMNESS — no dice, from the math library or from the platform's
 *     secure-random source. Same grep, and its `forbidden` list names both.
 *
 *  3. SET / MAP ITERATION ORDER — a `Map` is used for id lookup only and is
 *     never iterated to produce output. The one `Set` (unique depths) is
 *     drained into an array and then EXPLICITLY sorted numerically, so its
 *     insertion order cannot reach the result.
 *
 *  4. `Object.keys()` ORDER — never used. Nothing in the output is built by
 *     walking an object's keys.
 *
 *  5. LOCALE — locale-aware string comparison and the whole
 *     internationalization API are BANNED here. They vary with ICU build and
 *     host locale, which is exactly the "different machine, different bytes"
 *     failure this file exists to prevent. Id ties break on `compareIds`,
 *     plain UTF-16 code-unit comparison. (Same grep, same reason as 1.)
 *
 *  6. SORT STABILITY — never relied on. Every comparator is TOTAL: it falls
 *     through to the node id, which is unique, so no two elements ever
 *     compare equal and the engine's tie handling is unreachable.
 *
 *  7. FLOAT ACCUMULATION — there is none. No coordinate is ever computed by
 *     adding a step to the previous coordinate. Every one is
 *     `origin + index * step` from integer constants, so the value depends on
 *     the index alone and not on how many nodes were summed before it.
 *
 *  8. NEGATIVE ZERO — `Math.round(-0.2)` is `-0`, which is `!== 0` under
 *     `Object.is` and can flip a snapshot comparison for no visible reason.
 *     `snap()` normalizes it away.
 *
 *  9. NON-FINITE INPUT — a `NaN` or `Infinity` depth would poison every
 *     downstream coordinate and propagate silently. `finiteDepth()` clamps
 *     to a deterministic integer instead.
 *
 * 10. INPUT ARRAY ORDER — split deliberately in two:
 *
 *       `graph.nodes` order IS meaningful and IS preserved. It is the user's
 *       authoring order, and `tests/determinism.test.ts` already states the
 *       rule: "does NOT ignore array order — arrangement is the user's".
 *       Node ordinal is array index, on purpose.
 *
 *       `graph.edges` order is NOT meaningful. Edges are derived from the
 *       node walk, so their array position carries nothing the node list does
 *       not already say. Edges are therefore deduplicated and sorted on an
 *       explicit total key before any geometry is computed. Shuffling the
 *       edge array is byte-identical — covered by a test.
 *
 * 11. DUPLICATE NODE IDS — `deriveMapGraph` cannot produce them today (folder
 *     ids are unique), but the type permits it. First occurrence wins for
 *     edge lookup; every node still gets its own ordinal from its own index.
 *     Documented rather than thrown on, because a layout that throws takes
 *     the whole map down over a drawing detail.
 *
 * 12. DANGLING EDGES — an edge naming a job that is not in `nodes` is dropped,
 *     deterministically, and counted in `dropped` so the caller can see it
 *     rather than wonder where a cable went.
 *
 * Every number this file emits is an integer. That is not decoration: it is
 * what makes the output survive a JSON round trip byte for byte, with no
 * float formatting to argue about. `tests/determinism.test.ts` asserts it.
 */

DOC GENERATOR — NOTCH GRAPH

Spec, Map: "Node/edge graph with lines and notches (emphasizing timeline)".
The second of the two styles over the SAME geometry — switching to this
renderer moves nothing. `graph-layout.ts` is style-blind on purpose, so a
job sits at the identical coordinate in both views and the user is looking

What "emphasizing timeline" buys, concretely, and what cable does not have:

  - A ruler across the top, one tick per step in the sequence, numbered.
    Position along X is elapsed sequence, and here it is measured.
  - A rail per hierarchy lane, drawn only between the first and last job
    that actually sits in it (Guideline 9: the higher the parent, the more
    global the detail, and a rail shows how long a layer stays in play).
  - Right-angle runs between jobs instead of curves — a horizontal run
    reads as elapsed time in a way a bezier does not.
  - Jobs as notches cut across the rail, not circles floating on it.

Like `CableGraph`, this renders the contents of an `<svg>`, owns no
viewport, computes no layout, and takes its colors from `theme.css`.

characters is a live-typing UI concern (`taxonomy.screenLabel`), for a later
phase's input component to call before it ever reaches this store.

comments.text:
MOVES A NODE TO A DIFFERENT PARENT — Brandon, 2026-08-28.

`reorderChildren` above changes ORDER within one parent. This changes DEPTH:
it is what the docset panel's ←/→ buttons call (indent = become a child of
the sibling above; outdent = become a sibling of your own parent) and what a
drag onto a different folder calls. Same node `id` throughout, so any
selection or drag state pointing at it stays valid.

`index` is the position among the new parent's children AFTER this node has
been lifted out of wherever it was. That ordering matters when the new
parent is also the old one: lifting first, then inserting, is the only
reading under which "move to index 2" means the same thing regardless of
where the node started. Out-of-range values are CLAMPED, not refused — the
callers compute an index from a tree they have already read, and an
off-by-one there should land the node at an end, not throw at the user.

FOUR REFUSALS, all structural, none invented here:
  - The root cannot move. `types.ts`: "exactly one, at the top."
  - A file cannot become a parent. `DocsetFile` has no `children`.
  - A node cannot move into itself or its own descendant — that detaches
    the whole branch from the root, which is silent data loss, and the
    docset-icons task's rule is that nothing is destroyed silently.
  - An unknown node or parent id is a bug in the caller, not a user action.

Re-reading `shared/types.ts` and `shared/taxonomy.ts` closely before writing
a line of this file, because the instruction was to get the order semantics
right against them rather than invent new ones:

  - `taxonomy.renderDocument` iterates `template.segments`, NEVER
    `content.values`. `types.ts`'s own comment on `FileContent.values` says
    it outright: "the TEMPLATE decides order, never this array, so a
    reordered store cannot change a byte of output."

So this store does not own an ordering RULE of its own — the rule already
lives in taxonomy.ts and is correct. What this store owns instead:

  1. Upsert-by-`fieldId` semantics on every write, so `values` never holds
     two entries for the same field and there is never a "last one wins"
     case for the kernel to resolve in the first place.

     `values`) so any UI reading through this store sees fields in the one
     order that matters — feeding Phase 7 the same order the exporter uses,
     not a second, independently-invented one.
  3. `getAllContents`, which orders its OUTPUT array via
     `taxonomy.resolveDocset` — reusing the kernel's own depth-first,
     authoring-order walk — so the database this store hands to save-model
     is not sorted some third way.

comments.text:
THE `templateId` SEAM — A6 flagged it, Brandon assigned it to Phase 7.

Two fields carry a file's template: `DocsetFile.templateId` (structural, in
the docset tree) and `FileContent.templateId` (here). They are NOT
interchangeable, and the difference was a live bug, not a cosmetic one:

  - `taxonomy.planDocuments` — the exporter's plan — resolves the template
    from `file.templateId` ONLY (taxonomy.ts, the `templatesById.get` line).
    `renderDocument` never reads `content.templateId` at all.
  - `main/ipc/register.ts`'s `filesUsingTemplate` counts usage the same way.
  - `attachTemplate` used to write only `content.templateId`. So a file
    given a template in the editor still exported with `template === null`
    — i.e. as a plain file — while the preview showed the template.

RULING: `DocsetFile.templateId` is the single source of truth. It is what
the exporter reads and what persists in the docset tree. `FileContent`'s is
a mirror, kept in step here so the two cannot diverge: these two functions
are the only place a template is attached or detached, and each writes both
stores in one call. The docset write goes FIRST — if the project is not open
in `docset-store`, it throws before this store has been touched, so a
failure cannot leave the two halves disagreeing.

`FileContent.templateId` is not deleted because it is contract shape that
`project-db`, the main-process tests and the determinism tests all construct
— removing it is a kernel change with a much wider blast radius than the bug
warrants. See docs/reports/A7.md DECISIONS.

DOC GENERATOR — PROJECT STORE

Multiple projects open at the same time (Foundation 6). This is the one
place cross-store wiring happens for Phase 3: opening a project hydrates
`docset-store`, `editor-store`, `library-store` and `map-store` for it in
one call; closing releases all four. Later phases (App.tsx and beyond) only
need to call `openProject`/`closeProject` here and the rest of the renderer
state follows automatically.

`refreshProjects` (the `project:list` channel) is deliberately conservative:
it updates the known project list, but it does NOT re-hydrate the other
three stores for a project already tracked locally. `project:list` returns
each project's last-PERSISTED state from the main-process registry — if
this blindly re-hydrated on every call, an in-progress local edit (typed
into `editor-store`, not yet autosaved) would be silently overwritten by
the server's older copy. Only a project genuinely new to this renderer gets
hydrated from a list refresh.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — SAVE MODEL

Guideline 25: "Autosave. Forks with 'save as new'. Buttons: 'save', 'new',
'load', 'save as new'. New and load always ask whether to save or save as
new, regardless of autosave."

WHERE DIRTY TRACKING LIVES

`docset-store.ts` and `editor-store.ts` each keep a tiny per-project
revision counter, bumped on every local edit. This file is the only reader
of those counters: a project is dirty when either counter has moved since
this file last saved it. That is a cheap, exact signal — no deep-equality
walk of the tree on every keystroke — and it is why the "not saved since
the last edit" state is asked here, not read off `Project.save.dirty`
(which only reflects main's view as of the last `project:open` or explicit
`updateProject`, and this file is what keeps that fresher one, not the
other way round). A later phase's UI should read `isDirty`/`useDirty` here,
not the cached `Project.save` field.

AUTOSAVE DISCOVERS OPEN PROJECTS ON ITS OWN

Rather than requiring `project-store.ts` (or a future UI phase) to
remember to call a "start tracking" function on every open — a forgettable
step that would make autosave silently not apply to a project, exactly the
kind of silent failure this whole app is built to refuse — this file
watches `docset-store.getOpenProjectIds()` on every docset/editor change
and syncs its own tracked set to match. Autosave engages for a project the
moment it is hydrated, with no second call required.

"SAVE AS NEW" FLUSHES LIVE EDITS FIRST — A REAL FINDING, NOT A GUESS

Checked `main/ipc/register.ts`'s `project:saveAsNew` handler before writing
this: it forks `project.database` — the REGISTRY's last-persisted copy —
and does not accept a `docsetRoot`/`contents` payload at all (see
`SaveAsNewRequest` in `ipc-contract.ts`). Calling it directly while the
renderer holds unsaved edits would fork the OLD state and silently drop
whatever the user just typed. `saveAsNew` below calls `save()` first for
exactly this reason.

absence is the enforcement — `tests/export-rules.test.ts` asserts it stays
absent, so a later agent cannot quietly add one.

PHASE 1 CONTRACT EXTENSION — Brandon's call, 2026-08-27.

The diff has to render the database side to compare it, and rendering
depends on what the user chose for the empty ones. Without this the diff
always assumed the default, so anyone exporting with `createEmptyDocuments`
ON saw their skeleton files reported as "on disk but not in the database" —
which points at "restore from the database", the choice that overwrites
their work.

renders the database side with the wrong inputs accuses the user's real
files of being strangers. Required, not optional — an empty document is
either expected or not, and the diff cannot guess which.

Guideline 13: "a job view on the docset viewer shows every document someone
doing a job will see along the hierarchy path."

The walk runs root-first, so the global layer arrives first and the job's own
documents arrive last — Guideline 9: the higher the parent, the more global
the detail.

At each folder on the path it collects that folder's own files, then the
files inside any `resource` folder hanging off it. That second part is
Guideline 9's other half: a child layer may contain folders that are not
instructions but global tools or the location of materials, "placed there
because it makes more sense than in individual files" — so a person doing the
job sees them along the path.

It does NOT reach into sibling sequence or job folders. Work belonging to a
different job is not on this job's path.

Returns `null` when the id is not a folder, or is a folder that is not a job.
Guideline 10 makes the job the endpoint of the taxonomy and the lens for
nodes; a job view of a non-job is not a thing.

comments.text:
Turns a template plus what the user typed into the exact text of a document.

Guideline 2 — no word comes from anywhere but the user's typing or a
template — is enforced by there being nowhere in this function that a string
literal is concatenated into `text`. Only `segment.text` (typed into the
template) and `body.text` (typed into a box, or the verbatim contents of an
attachment) ever reach the output.

An empty input emits NOTHING — no placeholder, no label, no blank line. A
placeholder would be the app putting a word in the document.

Line endings are normalized to LF (Brandon's call, 2026-08-27). That is the
only change made to user content: no trailing newline is added, nothing is
trimmed, no whitespace is collapsed.

Ordering comes from `template.segments` and never from `content.values`, so
a store that reorders its field values cannot change a single byte. Where a
field id appears twice in `values`, the last one wins — deterministically,
because `values` is an ordered array.

comments.text:
Guideline 24: "When a template is edited after maps use it, the app asks and
flags."

Brandon's call, 2026-08-27. The old drift test could only notice a file
holding a value for a field id the template no longer has — so ADDING or
REMOVING a box was caught, and rewording the fixed text between the boxes was
not. A wording-only edit changes the shape of every document authored from
the template and used to trip nothing at all.

This fingerprints what actually decides a document's bytes: the ordered
segments. Rewording a fixed segment changes it. Reordering changes it.
Renaming an input's LABEL changes it too — the label never reaches a document
(Guideline 2), but it is what the user reads when filling the box in, so a
file authored under the old wording was authored under a different question.

NOT included: `Template.name`, `createdAt`, and `revision` itself. None of
them affects what a document contains, and folding them in would report drift
for renaming a template in the library.

DERIVED, NOT STORED — flagged in A2's receipt. A `revisionId` field sitting on
`Template` would have to be recomputed by every code path that edits a
template, and forgetting one is exactly the silent-drift bug this is here to
fix. Computing it from the segments means it cannot go stale.

 * not. A wording-only edit changes the shape of every document authored from

 * Renaming an input's LABEL changes it too — the label never reaches a document

comments.text:
Decides the entire export before a byte is written.

Guideline 1, as amended by Brandon on 2026-08-27:

  options.createEmptyDocuments OFF (the default, and Guideline 1 as written)
    A file whose inputs are all empty produces NO document. It lands in
    `omissions` — and every omission carries `flagged: true`, because the
    caller must raise the Guideline 16 block for it. Silently producing
    nothing is the one behaviour that is not allowed.

  options.createEmptyDocuments ON
    The document is written anyway, marked `writtenEmpty`, so the user can
    see which files came out as skeletons. Asking for a skeleton on purpose
    is a legitimate thing to want from a run-skeleton generator.

Guideline 22: every omission, and every empty field inside a document that
WAS written, is carried out of here so the user gets told.

Guideline 20 is not this function's job — write-beside naming happens against
the real directory at write time, via `writeBesideName`. What this guarantees
is that the decision of WHAT to write never touches the disk.

DOC GENERATOR — SHARED TYPES

Docset + template + library + discrepancy shapes. One file, per the runmap.

Two rules govern everything in here:

  Guideline 2  No word in the output comes from anywhere but the user's
               typing or a template. Every `kind`, `role`, `reason` and
               `trigger` string below is INTERNAL. None of them is ever
               written into an exported document. Only `FixedTextSegment.text`
               (which the user typed into a template) and field values
               (which the user typed into a box) reach a file.

  Guideline 6  Exporting the same input twice, a week apart, is byte-identical.
               Therefore: no optional properties on anything that gets
               serialized. `JSON.stringify` silently drops `undefined` keys,
               so an optional property is a byte-difference waiting to happen.
               Absence is spelled `| null`, always.

DOC GENERATOR — PROJECT DATABASE

Map index + backup store + schema versions. The runmap folds `migrations.ts`
into this file; see SCHEMA below for why there is nothing to migrate yet.

Foundation 1: "Keep a database in the project folder that will be included in
the compile. Map index + the app's backup of the actual files. So files on
disk are what you see and edit; the database is what the app restores from
and diffs against."

WHY JSON AND NOT SQLITE — A2's call, flagged for Brandon.

A0 deliberately left `dependencies` empty and left the storage engine to this
phase. The database is canonical JSON on disk, written through
`taxonomy.canonicalJson`, for three reasons that come straight off the spec:

  1. Guideline 6 wants byte-identical output from identical input. A SQLite
     file is not byte-stable — page layout, free lists and vacuum state all
     drift — so every save would show a diff the user did not cause.
     `canonicalJson` sorts keys and spells `undefined` as `null` precisely so
     two equal states serialize to equal bytes. A1 wrote it for this.
  2. Foundation 1 says the database is "included in the compile" — it travels
     with the project folder. A text file survives being copied, zipped,
     versioned and read by a human. A binary needs the app to be legible.
  3. A native SQLite binding has to be rebuilt against every Electron ABI.
     That is a build hazard bought for a store that holds one document.

If the project ever outgrows a single JSON document, this is the file that
changes and nothing else — every other service goes through the functions
below rather than touching the disk.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — FILESYSTEM

Finder pick, project path resolution, and write-beside.

THIS IS THE FILE WHERE A PLAUSIBLE-LOOKING BUG DESTROYS THE USER'S WORK.
Two rules govern every function in it.

GUIDELINE 20 — "Every export is a new file written beside existing files.
Exports never overwrite anything."

  `taxonomy.writeBesideName` picks a free name from a SNAPSHOT of a
  directory listing. A snapshot is not a guarantee: between the listing and
  the write, anything on the machine can create that file. So no function
  here trusts a name check. Every create goes through `O_EXCL` — `wx` for a
  file, non-recursive `mkdir` for a directory — which is the kernel refusing
  to clobber, not this code promising not to. If the name is taken we get
  `EEXIST` and step aside; we never truncate.

  There is no function in this file that opens a user file for writing
  without `O_EXCL`. `atomicReplace` is the one overwriting write, it is
  private, and it is reachable only through two fenced entry points:
  `writeFileAtomic` (restricted to a project's own database folder by
  `assertAppOwned`) and `writeAppSettingsFileAtomic` (restricted to the app's
  own settings folder).

CONTAINMENT — a docset label is user text. `screenLabel` rejects `/` and
  NUL, but it does NOT reject `..`, so a folder labelled `..` resolves to a
  path outside the export root. Every path built from user text goes through
  `resolveWithin`, which refuses anything that escapes.

ELECTRON: this module is deliberately importable WITHOUT Electron. The only
Electron call (`pickFolder`) imports it dynamically at call time, so the
tests can exercise the dangerous code against a real temp directory without
booting an app.

 *   directory listing. A snapshot is not a guarantee: between the listing and

comments.text:
ROLLBACK IS THE ONLY REASON THESE TWO FUNCTIONS EXIST.

"No partial exports survive on disk, ever." A
failed export must delete everything it wrote this run and be treated as if
it never ran.

Deleting is the operation that loses work when it is aimed one directory too
high, so both functions below are deliberately the WEAKEST tools that do the
job:

    not glob, and does not take a directory.

(`export-service`) tracks the exact paths it created and hands them back one
at a time; nothing is inferred from a directory listing.

DOC GENERATOR — IPC REGISTRATION

Wires one handler to every channel in the contract.

THREE THINGS THIS FILE GUARANTEES STRUCTURALLY:

  1. Every channel has a handler. `Handlers` is a mapped type over
     `IpcChannel`, so a missing channel is a compile error here rather than a
     silent hang in the renderer three phases later.
  2. Nothing escapes as an exception. Every handler is wrapped; a throw comes
     back as `ok: false` with a code from the contract. An unhandled rejection
     across the IPC boundary would reach the renderer as a stringified stack.
  3. Guideline 16: `discrepancies` is on the envelope and is always an array.
     A handler cannot succeed "quietly" while something was renamed, replaced,
     emptied or stepped aside — the flags travel on success and failure alike.

at load time, so the wiring can be exercised without booting an app.

DOC GENERATOR — PRELOAD BRIDGE

The typed bridge. This is the only place the renderer can reach the main
process, and it exposes exactly the contract and nothing else.

WHY THE CHANNEL IS CHECKED AGAINST A LIST

`invoke` is typed to `IpcChannel`, but types are a compile-time promise and
this function sits at the boundary where untrusted renderer code runs. A
renderer that has been compromised — or a bug that builds a channel name from
a string — could pass anything at all. So the name is checked against the
runtime `IPC_CHANNELS` list before it is forwarded, and an unknown channel
comes back as a normal `ok: false` result rather than reaching `ipcMain`.

FOUNDATION 4: there is no channel here that runs anything, because there is
no such channel in the contract. This file cannot widen that surface — it can
only forward names the contract already lists.

Built as CommonJS on purpose (see `electron.vite.config.ts`): Electron does
not load an ESM preload when the renderer is sandboxed.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — APP SHELL

Root component, mounted here. This file owns LAYOUT ONLY —
three vertical stacks, drawers, splitters, project tabs, and the
dimmed-behind-modal library overlay.
This file provides one clearly-named placeholder `<div>` per
slot and nothing else — no panel logic, no panel state.

LAYOUT, PER SPEC (line 3 + WINDOWS section)

  "Map is the whole screen, docset and editor are tabs on the sides that
  open drawers, user gets to adjust the width of the borders (3 vertical
  stacks for windows)."

Three vertical stacks, left to right: docset drawer, map (always full
height, always mounted), editor drawer. Each drawer has a persistent tab
strip at the outer edge (always visible, toggles the drawer) and, when
open, a resizable panel between the tab strip and the map, dragged via a
`Splitter`. The docset drawer's own panel splits horizontally per spec
line 12: file list above, completed-file preview below, adjustable border
height — a second `Splitter` on the y axis, local to that drawer.

LIBRARY OVERLAY, PER SPEC (line 3)

  "Settings/archive/script editor is separate screen entirely (pop out
  that can be dragged around to see the map screen, but map screen is a
  kinda dark and can't be clicked on except for modal button in the bottom
  corner of the map screen that says 'save' or 'cancel' and closes the
  movable screen)."

No IPC channel or event for "library window open" exists in
`shared/ipc-contract.ts`. Read literally, the "pop out" is not a second OS
window — it's a draggable overlay panel within this same renderer, moved
by its own header, sitting above a dimmed backdrop that blocks every
click on the map screen except the two modal buttons. `isLibraryOpen` and
the overlay's drag position are therefore local state owned by this shell,
not a store — there is nothing for a store to synchronize with yet.

The spec's ONLY stated behavior for the Save/Cancel buttons is that they
"close the movable screen" — nothing about what "save" persists, because
that's library-internal state. So both buttons just close the
overlay here.

SPLITTERS AND DRAWER STATE ARE LOCAL, NOT STORE STATE

No store owns "is the docset drawer open" or "how wide is it" — those are
pure window-chrome concerns, not domain data, and nothing downstream reads
them. Kept as local `useState` in this component, same category call as
`AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`: arbitrary defaults, one constant each, cheap
to change.

PERSISTENCE — WIRED

This state survives a reload, and per spec line 22
settings live in a findable plain-text file ("stored somewhere else as
normal text files I could find if I needed to with finder") — NOT
`localStorage` (an opaque blob in Electron's user-data folder, the opposite
of findable) and NOT the project database (spec line 28 fences that to the
map index and file backups, and it ships in the compile).

So this file no longer stores chrome itself: it holds ONE `AppLayoutSettings`
value, reads it once on mount through `settings:readLayout`, and writes it
back through `settings:writeLayout` on a debounce. `main/services/
settings-service.ts` owns the file — WHERE that file lives is still
Brandon's open call, behind one constant there.

THE DEFAULTS LIVE HERE, NOT IN MAIN. Main returns only the fields that
survived reading the file (`StoredLayoutSettings`, a partial), and this file
merges them over `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` below and clamps them to the same
min/max the splitters enforce. One place that knows what a legal drawer
width is, and it is the one that draws the drawer. A missing file, a
corrupt file, or a failed read all land in the same place: the defaults,
silently, with the app still starting.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST READ COMES BACK (`isLayoutLoaded`).
Writing on mount would overwrite Brandon's saved layout with the defaults in
the one frame before his real values arrive.

DIM SCOPE — MAP SCREEN ONLY

The dimmed-behind-modal backdrop covers the map screen
(`.map-slot`) only, not the project tabs or either drawer — spec line 3's
"map screen is a kinda dark" is the map, not the whole working surface.
The backdrop and the Save/Cancel modal buttons are therefore rendered
INSIDE `.map-slot` (see `MapDimOverlay`), not as a full-viewport overlay.
The library window itself (the draggable pop-out) stays a top-level fixed
overlay — spec says it "can be dragged around to see the map screen",
which only makes sense if it can move over the drawers too.

CLOSE-TAB PROMPT — WIRED

Closing a project tab prompts the same way new and load
prompt. `'close'` is now
a first-class `SaveAction` member (`shared/types.ts`) and
`save-model.confirmClose` is its ask, identical in shape to
`confirmNew`/`confirmLoad`. `handleCloseProject` goes through it, and the
tab is closed only after the ask resolves.

THE PROMPT UI IS MINIMAL AND INLINE-STYLED, ON PURPOSE. `save-model`'s `decide`
callback is where that dialog will eventually plug in. Until then the ask
needs SOMETHING on screen or it is not an ask, so `SavePromptDialog` below
is the smallest honest one: the two choices the contract allows
(`SavePrompt.choices`), a name box for the fork, and a Cancel that abandons
the close entirely.

CANCEL IS NOT A THIRD CHOICE. `SaveModelChoice` has exactly two arms and the
contract has no "discard"; Cancel rejects out of `decide`, which means
nothing is saved AND nothing is closed — see `save-model.ts`'s note.

comments.text:
DOC GENERATOR — DOCSET PANEL

Mounts into `.docset-file-list-slot` (spec line 12: "Preview
of what filetree will look like on top half (scroll bar)... how to add
files and folders"). Owns the editable filetree: add / rename / delete /
reorder folders and files, tag folders and files for the map (spec,
WINDOWS: "Use tags on folders to tag and coordinate with nodes"), and
click-to-select for `FilePreview.tsx` in the slot below.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN
  - The split between file list and preview — `Splitter` +
    `docsetListHeight` in `App.tsx` already does this; this file is the
    top half's content only, not a second split.
  - The completed-file text and its tag editor — `FilePreview.tsx`, mounted
    separately into the slot below. This file only tracks and exposes
    WHICH node is selected, via `usePreviewSelection` below.
  - Template authoring/attachment — A file added here is always a
    Foundation-2 plain file (`templateId: null`) until the editor attaches
    one; `FilePreview.tsx` still renders it correctly either way.
  - Character screening enforcement beyond this UI — `docset-store.ts`'s
    own header says screening a label is "a live-typing UI concern... for
    a later phase's input component to call before it ever reaches this
    store." `LabelField` below is that component: it blocks Save on any
    Guideline-18 ERROR and shows WARNINGs inline, but does not build the
    full "this file / this happened / possible outcomes / deterministic
    choices" discrepancy block — that shared shape is `common/Dialogs.tsx`.

STYLING: no new CSS file — `theme.css` is outside this fence.
`.docset-file-list-slot` centers/italicizes as a PLACEHOLDER style; this
component overrides it with an inline style on its own root.

  - DRAG-AND-DROP reorder, on native HTML5 drag events and no dependency
    (`package.json`'s `dependencies` stays empty). See DRAG STATE below for
    what counts as a valid drop; everything else is a silent no-op, never
    an error. The ↑/↓ buttons are KEPT — same mutator, and they are the
    keyboard-reachable path that dragging is not.

  - Every row shows a LEADING KIND ICON (folder glyph / blank-page
    glyph, inline SVG — `FolderIcon`/`FileIcon` below) with three
    behaviors: click it swaps file<->folder
    (`docsetStore.swapNodeKind`); click the NAME selects the row;
    click-and-hold the icon drags, and a fired drag NULLS the
    swap — see `handleIconClick`'s `suppressSwapRef` guard below for how.
  - Folders (never the root — it stays pinned to `global`, no control at
    all) get a binary JOB TOGGLE: on = `role: 'job'`, off = the folder's
    remembered previous non-job role (`toggleFolderJobRole` below),
    defaulting to `'sequence'` when nothing was remembered yet.
  - The row is still the drop target.
  - Rename is UNCHANGED: it was never on the name click — it is still the
    explicit "Rename" button.

MOVING BETWEEN LEVELS, NOT JUST WITHIN ONE

  ←/→ BUTTONS, beside the ↑/↓ that were already there. → indents (become
  the last child of the sibling above); ← outdents (become the item right
  after your own parent, one level up). Disabled with a reason in the
  tooltip when there is nowhere to go: nothing outdents past the root, and
  nothing indents into a file. This is the keyboard-reachable path.

  DRAG, WIDENED. A row is now three drop zones — see the
  DRAG STATE block below. The highlight tells you which of the two things
  is about to happen BEFORE you release: an edge line means "beside this
  row, same level", a full ring around the row means "inside this folder,
  one level deeper".

Both paths call `docsetStore.moveNode` — one mutator, one set of refusals,
so the button and the drag cannot disagree about what is legal.

DOC GENERATOR — EDITOR PANEL

Mounts into `.editor-panel-slot` (App.tsx's `EditorDrawerPanel`).
Foundation 7: "the editor is where the files are edited or attached to the
folder" — this file edits whatever node `docset/DocsetPanel.tsx`'s tree has
selected, via the SAME shared `usePreviewSelection` store `FilePreview.tsx`
already reads. Click a file in the docset drawer and both the preview
below it AND this drawer update to that file — one selection, two views,
never two independently-invented ones.

WHAT IT OWNS
  - The template picker: attach / detach, through `editorStore.attachTemplate`
    / `detachTemplate` ONLY. `DocsetFile.templateId` is
    the single source of truth the exporter reads, and those two functions
    are the only place it may be written — this file never writes
    `FileContent.templateId` directly, and never calls `docset-store.ts`'s
    `setFileTemplate` itself.
  - Walking `editorStore.getOrderedFieldViews` (never `content.values`
    directly) so field order here is exactly the order
    `taxonomy.renderDocument` — and therefore the exporter and
    `FilePreview.tsx` — use. Guideline 6: one order, not a second one
    invented for editing.
  - Dispatching each segment to the matching widget in `FieldInputs.tsx`:
    `fixed` -> read-only, `input`+`text` -> free text, `input`+`attachment`
    -> drop/import. This file has no rendering logic of its own for a
    field's VALUE — only for which widget a segment gets.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN
  - The widgets themselves — `FieldInputs.tsx`.
  - Tags — `FilePreview.tsx`'s `TagEditor` already covers files and
    folders alike; duplicating it here would be a second, independently
    invented tag UI for the same field (Guideline 6).
  - The completed-document TEXT — `FilePreview.tsx` calls
    `taxonomy.renderDocument` and shows the result; this file shows the
    INPUTS that feed it, not the rendered output. A one-line drift note
    (Guideline 24) is the only overlap, informational only — the full
    "this file / this happened / possible
    outcomes / deterministic choices" block is `common/Dialogs.tsx`.

STYLING: no new CSS file — `theme.css` is outside this fence.
`.editor-panel-slot` is a PLACEHOLDER style (centered, italic) meant for
the mount-point text, not real content; this component overrides on its
own root `<div>`, `.map-slot` /
`.docset-file-list-slot`. Unlike those two, `.editor-panel-slot` has no
`overflow: auto` of its own (theme.css), so this root sets it explicitly.

The typed wrapper over `main/preload.ts`'s bridge. Nothing else in the
renderer is allowed to touch `window.docGenerator` directly — every store in
`state.ts` goes through `invoke`/`call`/`onEvent` here.

GUIDELINE 16, THE PART THAT LIVES HERE

`IpcResult` always carries `discrepancies`, on success and failure alike.
That envelope is only as good as the promise that nothing built on top of it
drops the array on the floor. This file is where that promise is kept: every
`invoke()` feeds its `discrepancies` into a single feed, and the
`discrepancy:raised` event (for anything flagged outside a request the
renderer made) feeds the same one. Phase 9's `common/Dialogs.tsx` is the
eventual UI for this feed; this file only guarantees nothing reaches that UI
having already been quietly discarded.

The event listener is wired LAZILY, on the first `subscribeDiscrepancies`
call, not at module load. Importing this file must be side-effect-free —
under vitest (no bridge, no `window.docGenerator`) or during any renderer
bootstrap ordering, importing the module should never throw. Only calling
into it should.

DOC GENERATOR — LIBRARY WINDOW

Phase 8's first file. Spec: "the most underdeveloped window[]" — Brandon is
fine with that, and this file does not try to outgrow it.

SETTLED SHAPE, NOT REOPENED HERE: A4 already built the pop-out — an
in-renderer draggable overlay (`App.tsx`'s `LibraryWindow` function, the
drag header, `.library-window` CSS) with the map dimmed behind it
(`MapDimOverlay`) and Save/Cancel as two modal buttons in the map's bottom
corner. This file is the CONTENT mounted into that overlay's
`.library-window-slot` (`data-slot="library-window"`) — not a second
window, not new IPC for window management, not a redesign. `App.tsx`'s own
top-level function is also named `LibraryWindow`; the mount aliases the
import (`LibraryWindowContent`) rather than touch that file beyond the one
import + one slot-body line the fence allows.

SAVE/CANCEL — what A4's two modal buttons actually do today (per its own
file header): both just close the overlay. `library-store.ts`'s own header
explains why nothing here needed a buffered save: "READ-THROUGH, NOT
LOCAL-THEN-SAVED... every `library:*` write handler ALREADY persists to
disk and returns the resulting value before this store ever sees it."
Every action below (pick a folder, resolve a foreign file, fork a version)
commits the moment its own button is pressed — the same immediate-commit
pattern `docset/DocsetPanel.tsx`'s `LabelField`/tag editor/role select
already established. Closing the overlay (either modal button) simply
stops editing; there is nothing buffered to roll back, so "Cancel"
doing exactly what "Save" does is correct here, not a gap this file needs
to close. `ScriptEditor.tsx`'s propose/commit/discard flow (Guideline 5)
is the one place a DRAFT exists before it is persisted, and it owns its
own explicit commit/discard, independent of the overlay's buttons.

SETTINGS FOLDER PICKERS — Foundation 1 / Guideline 21: "a folder picked
from settings, through the Finder." The IPC channel already exists
end-to-end (`dialog:pickFolder`, `FolderPurpose = 'library-folder'`,
wired since A2) — this file is its first caller. `library.folderPath` is
shown with a "Choose Folder…" button; `library.backupPath` is shown
read-only (Guideline 21: the app compiles the backup itself, there is
nothing to pick).

FOREIGN FILES — Guideline 21: "add, ignore, or keep flagged — no fourth
choice." `library.foreignFiles` (`files-vs-database`, Foundation 1) is
listed with those exact three buttons, wired to
`libraryStore.resolveForeignFile`, which is the whole surface — no fourth
choice is offered here either.

VERSIONS — Guideline 4: "runs differ only by library version, labeled by
version name and date forked." `library-store.ts`'s `forkVersion` already
sets the new version ACTIVE on fork (no separate "switch version" channel
exists) — this file's version list is therefore a history, and "Fork new
version" is the only version control here.

TABS — Scripts (`ScriptEditor.tsx`) and Templates & Notes
(`NotesAndTemplates.tsx`) are the other two Phase 8 files; this file only
switches between them, owning no editing logic of its own for either.
